source.original_title: 06/10/2026 - Jonn Nolitt x Andrew Musial KFS
source.display_title: 06/10/2026 - Jonn Nolitt x Andrew Musial KFS  — Closed

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: I spoke with Kim. He spoke with you a few days ago, correct?

prospect.name: Jonn Nolitt
prospect.occupation: Retired; former global executive at Oracle 1996-2019 (700 employees across 40 countries, ~$90M annual budget)
prospect.training_background: X3 resistance-band system for 4.5 years after coming down from ~35% body fat; carnivore 4.5 years; 10 years vegan before that; ran track and played football/baseball in youth; four-day split on a six-week cycle; no gym membership, trains at home
prospect.medical: Achilles injury ~7 months ago from an unwarmed sprint, still not fully healed ('it hurts just a little when I squeeze it'); shoulder dislocated twice playing baseball, audible clicking he attributes to cartilage, no surgery; running a stack of ~10 research peptides (retatrutide, MOTS-C, CJC-1295, ipamorelin, SS-31, GHK-Cu, BPC/TB, KPV, tesamorelin, NAD+, epitalon); explicitly refuses medical care ('I don't do surgery on any ... I'm not a doctor guy')

signals: 9.9% body fat, biohacking room planned, sauna-space infrared, peptide protocol, Hume scale visceral fat tracking
Goal is 187 lb -> 210 lb at 6.5-7% body fat: marginal gains, not rescue
Spends '1,500, 2,000' a month on supplements; price surprise but no price resistance

goals.text: Get to 210 lb bodyweight at 6.5-7% body fat, with an interim step at 195 lb
Add a new training stimulus his body has not seen, to break past what X3 alone can deliver
See how far he can push biological optimisation and cellular regeneration - 'you're either degenerating or regenerating'
Resolve the shoulder clicking so overhead movement works properly

pains.text: Last ~4 lb of abdominal fat will not shift on the current programme
Shoulder clicks in the AC/overhead position from two old dislocations; overhead pressing used to hurt
Achilles still not fully recovered seven months after the tear; cannot sprint on hard ground
Cannot tell whether kettlebells will build muscle as fast as the system he already trusts

objections.raw_quote: Oh, . I didn't know it was that much. Can you break that up at all?
objections.rep_response: Immediately offered a 50/50 split - half now, half in 30 days, no interest - and sent a second payment link. No isolation question, no financial-picture questions.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, we'll see. That could be harder. I think that'd be a lot harder in the workout, but let's see what it is.
objections.rep_response: Moved straight into scheduling the onboarding call rather than addressing the doubt.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two-pay: $3,000 now, $3,000 in 30 days, stated as no interest. Separate split-payment link issued live.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: The program is also backed by a performance guarantee. So we established like a strength baseline in week one. So the commitment is to add at least eight kilograms to your core kettlebell lifts in six months... If you, for some reason wouldn't hit it, if you follow the exact protocols and everything, Trevor is going to work longer until you hit it.

evidence: Card entered live on the split-payment link; rep corrected a typo in the prospect's email mid-checkout
Onboarding call with Trevor booked and confirmed by email for Tuesday 11:15 a.m. Pacific
Counter-evidence: the client agreement email never arrived during the call ('Do you got the one with the agreement, too?' - 'No.'), so nothing was signed
Counter-evidence: prospect only registered the price after the first link was sent - 'I didn't know it was that much'
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor; rep to chase the unreceived agreement email for signature.

notable.note: Prospect is an unmedicated 60-ish retiree self-administering ~10 research peptides including retatrutide, with a partially healed Achilles tear and an unrepaired shoulder, who states flatly that he does not use doctors. The rep engaged with the peptide stack as a peer and interested consumer rather than raising any caution, and never asked whether anyone had cleared him for loaded overhead kettlebell work. Equipment (kettlebells) was disclosed as an extra cost only after the card was being entered, to a prospect with no gym.

quality.notes: Attribution inverts repeatedly - several of the rep's discovery questions are labelled 'Jonn1' and several of the prospect's answers are labelled as the rep (e.g. 00:06:11, 00:13:51, 00:46:00). Roles were read from content throughout. The rep's Fathom label reads 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the folder and title name him Andrew Musial; treated as the same person (Poland-based closer).
